correctness.rationale: For every positive even n, each 2-species site is exactly an unordered pair edge, with pair multiplicities s_ij and fixed cubic species degrees. The identity sum s_ij=m and s^2=s+2 choose(s,2) proves the affine C-score formula. Coefficient expansion enumerates all degree-three loopless multigraph pair multiplicities with weight 1/product(s_ij!), and multiplying by m! restores labeled sites; hence the all-n null generating law is exact. At n=4, opposite edges have equal multiplicities a,b,c with sum 3, giving the exhaustive types (1,1,1),(2,1,0),(3,0,0), and counts 720,1080,60. A separate ordered-column brute force enumerates all 6^6=46656 possible assignments and reproduces the constrained table. At n=2 only one matrix exists. So strict upper-tail significance at 0.05 first occurs at n=4 with probability 1/31. No finite computation is substituted for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The consulted original ecological papers establish the C-score, alternative degree-two tiny enumerations, simulation-based fixed-margin comparisons, and the importance of uniform matrix sampling; none gives the stated 3-by-2 all-size exact finite null law or the sharp four-species p-value. A mathematically relevant result on degree-two regular cycle statistics concerns a different graph degree and does not directly cover these cubic multigraph coefficients. Multiple exact-title, definition, and reduction searches of published research records returned no matching claim. Residual risk: some general multigraph-coefficient enumeration may imply this law after a nontrivial translation, and some ecological text remains inaccessible. This self-review is not independent confirmation.

value.rationale: The exact distribution is a natural statistical calibration for species co-occurrence null tests. It explicitly distinguishes uniform labeled matrices from nonuniform sampled classes, computes tail probabilities without Monte Carlo error for every even n within a common sparse margin family, and resolves the first possible strict 5% significant design as four species and six sites with exact 1/31 null probability. This is a motivated exact null law and sharp minimal sampling configuration rather than a random slice of a graph census. The work does not infer biological competition, and general computation remains exponential.
